The fluid.dataset~ object is central to the FluCoMa data analysis objects. It is used for storing many data points, each of which will be attached to an identifier, also known as a key. All of the data points in a dataset must have the same number of dimensions
Finally, you can swap the order of the entries in the labelset. This is convenient to retrieve from an original identifier on what frame/channel a point/item will be found
A fluid.dataset~ can be converted to a buffer too.

By default, each point/item is layed out framewise, so the 0th frame is 
the first item, where each dimension is a channel.
When tobuffer <buffer> 1 is passed, the copying is transposed. This means each channel will hold a point, and each frame will represent a dimension.
You can provide an optional number (0 or 1) to change the transposition of the copying, and an optional labelset to get.
tobuffer messages copies the contents of the dataset to the buffer provided as an argument.
displays the 9 nearest neighbours as symbols. They can be converted to numbers using `fromsymbol`

A fluid.dataset~ can be queried with an input point to return the nearest match to that point. Note: This feature is can be computationally expensive on a large dataset, as it needs to compute the distance of the queried point to each point in the dataset. If you need to perform multiple nearest neighbour queries on a fluid.dataset~ it is recommended to use fluid.kdtree~. This facility is most useful with smaller, ephemeral datasets such as those returned by fluid.datasetquery~
make a point on the poltter to query
dump the simple grid dataset to see its content
Finally, you can provide a labelset that will associate each channel to an identifier.
A fluid.dataset~ can be created from the contents of a buffer.

By default, each row is layed out framewise, so all of channel 1 is ordered in time as the columns of identifier 0.

When frombuffer <buffer> 1 is passed (implicitly 0), the copying is transposed. This means each identifier will contain the same index across all channels as the columns of a given identifier.
You can provide an optional number (0 or 1) to change the transposition of the copying.
frombuffer messages copies the contents of the buffer you provide as an argument to the dataset.

You can merge the points in one dataset with another. If the dataset you call merge on already has a key existing in the dataset you want to merge, the caller's will be preserved. Any keys not found in the dataset to merge will be added to the caller.
